prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

"Reddit By Danny Parisi Aug 23, 2022 Madewell launched its latest ad campaign on Tuesday, called “When the Fit Hits.” Under CMO Derek Yarbrough, the campaign is meant to appeal to both Madewell’s growing Gen-Z demo and its existing millennial core audience. Yarbrough said one of the key aspects of the brand’s marketing strategy is to tailor campaigns to fit the platform they’re premiering on."

[P5] source: https://www.glossy.co/fashion/how-madewell-is-navigating-tiktok-instagram-and-youtube/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The celebrities anchor the main campaign, starring in short videos showing off pieces from the fall denim collection. "Access and Perks: Insider loyalty benefits reinforce affordability perceptions through targeted offers, birthday rewards, and early access windows. TikTok supports discovery moments, fit try-ons, and staff styling, encouraging community participation with approachable prompts. Branded emails connect storytelling to commerce through clear CTAs, style bundles, and loyalty earn messaging."

[P7] source: https://www.latterly.org/madewell-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Denim Donation Events: Store activations with Cotton’s Blue Jeans Go Green exchange worn jeans for credit, driving store traffic and denim trade-ups. * Madewell Forever: Resale listings curated with ThredUp extend lifecycle storytelling, encouraging value-minded shoppers to reenter the funnel. * Insider Drops: Limited capsules, early access, and double-point denim periods concentrate urgency around seasonal launches. * Hometown Heroes Pop-ups: Local maker showcases position stores as cultural spaces, strengthening neighborhood relevance and word of mouth. The result is a brand story that pairs craft and community with tangible services."

[P8] source: https://thebigmarketing.com/madewell-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"This dynamic content keeps the website fresh and engaging, ultimately driving traffic and conversions. ### Utilizing Social Media for Engagement Madewell actively utilizes social media platforms to engage with its audience. The brand adopts a conversational approach, promoting direct interaction through comments and user-generated content. This not only builds community but also fosters brand advocacy among loyal customers. Instagram is a pivotal platform for Madewell, featuring high-quality visuals and stories that resonate with their audience. Engaging posts invite followers to participate in campaigns, share their own experiences, and showcase styling techniques."

[P9] source: https://thebigmarketing.com/madewell-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"How has Madewell leveraged social media as part of its overarching marketing strategy? Madewell uses social media to engage directly with customers and promote its brand values. Platforms like Instagram showcase user-generated content and brand storytelling. This approach builds a community around the brand and enhances customer connection."

[P10] source: https://www.latterly.org/madewell-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2024 | published: unknown
"Marketing Mix of Madewell Madewell’s marketing mix blends product excellence, price discipline, channel reach, and promotional precision to support profitable growth. The model prioritizes direct commerce while sustaining select wholesale partners for discovery and geographic breadth. Execution focuses on reliable value storytelling that emphasizes fit, durability, and style longevity. Analysts estimate Madewell generated approximately 850 million dollars in 2024 revenue, reflecting steady store productivity and resilient ecommerce demand. Growth levers include fit-driven launches, loyalty monetization, and circular resale integrations that attract value-conscious shoppers."
